2  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the order and award dated 26.03.2010 passed in WCA/FCR/81/2007 by the Labour Officer and Commissioner for Workmen Compensation, Chitradurga District, Chitradurga, on the ground that the deceased was not an employee under respondent No.1.
2.

Brief facts of the case are:-
Respondents No.2 to 7 being the claimants have filed claim petition before the learned Commissioner under the provisions of Employees Compensation Act by making averments that the deceased was working as a driver in the lorry bearing Registration No.TN-28-7507 under the employment of respondent No.1 and on 16.8.2007 when the deceased was proceeding from Chitradurga to Hospete, drove the said lorry in a rash and negligent manner and at that time the lorry bearing Registration No.HR-55-B-3607 was coming from Hospete to Chitradurga with high speed and both lorries have colluded with each other and in the said accident the deceased died.

Therefore, the claimants being the legal representatives have filed a claim petition for claiming NC: 2023:KHC:21523 compensation by invoking provisions of Employees Compensation Act stating that the deceased was working as a driver under the employment of respondent No.1 and the learned Commissioner after hearing the claim petition, granted the compensation holding both respondent No.1 and Insurance Company are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and because of the Insurance Policy directed the appellant/Insurance Company to indemnify respondent No.1/owner and pay the compensation.

3. Heard learned counsel from both sides and perused the materials on record.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that the deceased was not under the employment of respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 has not engaged the deceased as a driver, as an employee under him.

Therefore submitted that, there is no relationship of employer and employee between respondent No.1 and the deceased and appellant-Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1 in case of some other employee, as the deceased was not under the employment of respondent No.1.
NC: 2023:KHC:21523
Therefore, prays to allow the appeal by setting aside the order and award passed by the learned Commissioner.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondents No.2 to 7-claimants supported the impugned order and award passed by the learned Commissioner by stating that the deceased was an employee being a driver under respondent No.1-employer and therefore prays to dismiss the appeal.
6. Respondent No.1-owner remained absent in spite of service of notice to him.
Therefore, the learned Commissioner has placed respondent No.1 as exparte.

Then upon perusing the complaint New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri R Neetiraj on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40613154/
3 averments annexed to FIR-Ex.P1 given by cleaner of the lorry bearing No.TN-28-7507 stating that he has worked as a cleaner in the said lorry.

sentences.text: It is further stated in the first information statement given before the police that on 15.8.2007 one Rajesab resident of Salem is the driver in the said lorry.
On 15.08.2007 the said lorry has carried fan materials from Madras to Chitradurga and on the night of 15.08.2007 the load of fan materials was unloaded.

It is further stated that on 16.8.2007 at morning 5.00 a.m. one driver Rajesab (the deceased herein) belonging to Mubarak Transport NC:
2023:KHC:21523 Office and resident of Chirtradurga Town has taken the lorry for loading Ragi crop at Hospete and proceeded towards Hospete on the morning at 5.00 a.m. on 15.8.2007 and met with an accident with another lorry as stated above.
Thus, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The first information statement attached to Ex.P1-FIR is the only document available on record in the present case to prove whether the deceased was an employee under the employment of respondent No.1 or not.

In this context, upon the averments made in the first information statement above discussed, it is the contention of the Insurance Company that the deceased was not employee of respondent No.1, but was employed as a driver belonging to one Mubarak Transport Office situated at Chitradurga.

In this regard, the learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SANJEEV KUMAR SAMRAT Vs. NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS reported in 2013 ACJ 1.

entities.text: SANJEEV KUMAR SAMRAT Vs. NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND OTHERS reported in 2013 ACJ 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the facts are that a truck was hired on 12.4.2000 for carrying iron rods and cement by one Durga Singh, who was traveling with the goods along with two of his labourers.

When the vehicle was moving through Khara NC: 2023:KHC:21523 Patthar to Malethi, about 4.30 p.m. it met with an accident, as a consequence of which the two labourers, namely, Nagru Ram and Desh Raj sustained injuries and eventually succumbed to the same.

7. The legal representatives of said two labourers namely Nagru Ram and Desh Raj have filed respective claim petitions and it was heard by the Tribunal on the ground that the said risk of death of the said Nagru Ram and Desh Raj was covered as per the insurance policy, as the policy covered six employees and accordingly fastened the liability on the insurer.
The insurer has filed an appeal before the High Court of Himachal Pradesh.

The High Court held that so far as Durga Singh who is the owner of the goods is concerned, was traveling along with the goods and therefore, the Insurance Company was liable to pay the compensation to the legal representatives of Durga Singh.
But so far as the death of two labourers who are Desh Raj and Nagru Ram, the Insurance Company is not liable, but the owner of the lorry is liable to pay the compensation.
Therefore, the owner of the lorry had preferred an appeal before the Hon'ble Apex Court.

The Hon'ble NC: 2023:KHC:21523 Apex Court upon making analysis of the facts therein has held at paragraph No.24 as follows:
"24.
It is worthy to note that sub-clause (i)(c) of the proviso refers to an employee who is being carried in the vehicle covered by the policy.
Such vehicle being a goods carriage, an employee has to be covered by the statutory policy.

On an apposite reading of Sections 147 and 167 the intendment of the legislature, as it appears to us, is to cover the injury to any person including the owner of the goods or his authorized representative carried in a vehicle and an employee who is carried in the said vehicle.
It is apt to state here that the proviso commences in a different way.
A policy is not required to cover the liability of the New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Sri R Neetiraj on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40613154/

sentences.text: 4 employee except an employee covered under the 1923 Act and that too in respect of an employee carried in a vehicle.
To put it differently, it does not cover all kinds of employees.

Thus, on a contextual reading of the provision, schematic analysis of the Act and the 1923 Act, it is quite limpid that the statutory policy covers only the employees of the insured, either employed or engaged by him in a goods carriage.

It does not cover any other kind of employee and, therefore, someone who travels not being an NC: 2023:KHC:21523 authorized agent in place of the owner of goods, and claims to be an employee of the owner of goods, cannot be covered by the statutory policy and to hold otherwise would tantamount to causing violence to the language employed in the statute.
Therefore, we conclude that the insurer would not be liable to indemnify the insured."

8. Therefore, upon a conjoint reading of Sections 147 and 167 of the Motor Vehicle Act and the provisions of Employees Compensation Act, 1923, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the owner only in case the owner has engaged the services of the employee, but not the risk is covered of some other employees of other owner.

Therefore, in the present case,
considering the facts and circumstances as discussed above, regarding relationship of employer and employee, whether the deceased was employee of respondent No.1 upon analyzing the complaint averments, the deceased was belonging to one Mubarak Transport office who was working as driver in the said office and has taken lorry bearing No.TN-28-7507 and met with an accident.

Even though respondent No.1 may be the owner of the lorry bearing No.TN- - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21523 28-7507, but the owner is a resident of Tamil Nadu State and the lorry was in Chitradurga Town and the deceased was working as a driver in Mubarak Transport office at Chitradurga, as the deceased was also a resident of Chitradurga Town has taken the lorry and met with an accident.
Therefore, it is proved that the deceased was not the employee of respondent No.1.
Further more, there is no evidence on record produced by the claimants to prove that respondent No.1 - owner of the lorry has engaged the services of the deceased as a driver in the lorry.
On the way, if some other person has instructed the deceased and the deceased met with an accident, the owner of the lorry cannot be said that he is an employer of the said deceased.
Therefore, the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanjeev Kumar Samrat case supra, is squarely applicable to the case on hand.
Therefore, the relationship of employer and employee between respondent No.1 and the deceased is not proved.
When there is no relationship proved between the employer and employee, then the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the owner- respondent No.1.

Therefore, the findings made by the learned Commissioner in this regard are perverse and contrary to the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21523 evidence on record and the appeal filed by the insurance company is liable to be allowed, as there is no proof proving the relationship of employer and employee.
